- Any HTML in a polled feed becomes `post.cooked` unchanged and is emitted by `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20`, so a hostile or compromised feed serves scripts on the forum's own origin. The Readability path applies a tag allowlist; the RSS path applies nothing, which contradicts the stated intent that imported content must not escape validation. Put one `Sanitize.clean` (the `sanitize` gem is already a dependency) inside `TopicEmbed.import` with the allowlist the Readability path already uses, so every caller inherits it.

- The `imported_from` footer builds `<a href='#{url}'>` with no escaping, and the only guard is the unanchored `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` on line 11, which permits a quote in the query string. A URL ending `?a='/onmouseover='alert(1)` breaks out of the attribute in a post whose output is rendered raw. Escape with `CGI.escapeHTML(url)` and tighten the guard to `URI.parse(url).is_a?(URI::HTTP)`.

- `rss.items.each` has no rescue and calls `i.content.scrub` unconditionally. An RSS 2.0 item carrying only `<description>` gives `nil.scrub`, and one such item abandons every remaining item for that hourly run. Fall back across `content` / `description`, skip blank bodies, and wrap the loop body in rescue/next. Note `String#scrub` needs Ruby 2.1, so drop it or guard it.

- Wrapping `PostCreator#create` in an outer `Topic.transaction` makes the inner transaction a joined, non-savepoint one, so the `ActiveRecord::Rollback` PostCreator raises is swallowed and `create` still returns the unsaved post. `post.present?` is then true and `TopicEmbed.create!` inserts `post_id: nil` into a `null: false` column. Drop the outer transaction and test `post.persisted?`, not `post.present?`.

- `import_remote` is reached only from `topic_retriever.rb:52` and `disqus.thor:148`, and no spec touches it, so the Readability wiring and the `opts[:title] || doc.title` branch are entirely unexercised. Add a spec that stubs the fetch and asserts `.import` receives the parsed title and content.

- `'//cdn.example.com/x.jpg'.start_with?('/')` is true, so a protocol-relative asset is rewritten to `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x.jpg` and every such image or link in imported content breaks. Add `&& !href.start_with?('//')` to both rewrites and cover the case.

- On the PostgreSQL 9.x this era targets, a NOT NULL column with a default forces a full rewrite under `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` on the largest table in a Discourse install. Split into add (nullable, no default), batched backfill reusing the retry loop already in `migrate_word_counts.rb`, then `change_column_null`.

- This migration shipped before this branch; adding `force: true` makes it emit `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` on any `db:migrate:redo` or replay, silently destroying that table's data, while existing databases never re-run it at all. Revert the `force: true` -- it is a one-line deletion. If forcing is genuinely wanted, it belongs in a new timestamped migration.

- The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and the category lookup, and `import_remote` threads no category anywhere, so existing `-c` invocations now fail as an unknown switch and imported topics land uncategorized. Thread an optional `category:` through `import_remote` and `import` into the internal `PostCreator.new`.

- **Decision gate.** A single embed lookup re-downloads and re-upserts the entire feed inside a per-request worker, and the `feed_key` defined at `poll_feed.rb:20` that would make a conditional fetch possible is never used. Two defensible directions: drop the RSS pre-check and let `fetch_http` handle single-URL retrieval, or keep it and finish `feed_key` as a Last-Modified/ETag guard. Pick one before the rest of this group is worth optimizing.

- `topic_retriever_spec.rb:33-34` and `:39-40` stub both `perform_retrieve` and `retrieved_recently?`, so the test named for the throttle never runs the redis logic and nothing ever executes `perform_retrieve`. Stub the collaborators instead and assert the real outcome.

- `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false, so `execute`'s guard short-circuits on the first condition; both tests would still pass with the `feed_polling_url` and `embed_by_username` checks deleted. Stub the preceding conditions to true in each test so it isolates the condition it names.

- Every spec replaces `poll_feed` with a mock, so the fetch, parse, and per-item import logic has zero executed coverage -- which is why defects #4, #17, and #19 are invisible to CI. Add a fixture-driven spec covering a normal item, a blank-link item, and a non-http link.

- `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` has no separator or normalization, and nothing in the diff documents a trailing-slash requirement, so an integrator setting `http://forum.example.com` silently gets `http://forum.example.comembed/best`. Strip trailing slashes and insert the `/` explicitly.

- Any request that passes the spoofable Referer check enqueues a retrieval, and the only throttle keys on the exact URL string, so varying query strings on the embeddable host yields unbounded outbound fetches and one new topic per distinct URL from unauthenticated callers. Add a `RateLimiter` keyed on `request.remote_ip` for anonymous callers and key the throttle on host as well as URL.

- Both `poll_feed.rb:29` and `topic_embed.rb:48` hand a String to `Kernel#open`, whose pipe and local-file fallbacks are reachable; the scheme check in `import` runs only after the fetch, and `disqus.thor:148` feeds it links parsed from an externally supplied Disqus XML export. Parse to a `URI::HTTP` first and pass the URI object, which removes the fallback entirely.

- The feed path CGI-unescapes raw content and stores it as a `raw_html` post with no `Sanitize` call anywhere, even though the gem is already a dependency. Same fix as #1; doing it once in `TopicEmbed.import` covers both.

- `open(url).read` has no rescue and no explicit timeouts on the request-driven path. OpenURI raises on any non-2xx, a routine outcome for an arbitrary embed URL, so the job crashes and retries instead of returning nil, and `fetch_http` has no way to record a permanent failure. Rescue network and parse errors, set timeouts, and return nil.

- SETNX and EXPIRE are two separate commands; a crash or connection error between them leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no TTL, so `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever and that URL can never be imported again. Use the atomic `$redis.set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)` -- redis 3.0.6 in the lockfile supports it -- and release the key when the work fails.

- `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs unguarded before `fetch_http`, so any exception from the feed fetch, parse, or a single malformed item propagates and the on-demand HTTP retrieval never runs. Wrap the opportunistic poll in rescue-and-log, or enqueue it asynchronously.

- Nothing records that a URL can never be imported, so the controller re-enqueues on every reload and the iframe loops on the loading view indefinitely. Persist a failure marker alongside the existing throttle key and render a distinct error view when it is set.

- `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` searches the wrong direction and matches on substrings, so a shorter attacker origin contained in the URL passes. Normalize `discourseUrl` to a bare origin once, compare with `!==`, and also check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

- The reload is unconditional with no attempt cap, and each reload re-enqueues a job, so a URL that can never import polls forever. Cap at roughly five attempts and render a link to the forum instead.
- `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` runs after both branches, so a shared cache can serve "Loading Discussion..." for a minute after the topic exists. Move it inside the `if topic_id` branch.

- The update branch calls `PostRevisor.new(embed.post)` with no nil check, so re-importing an article whose post was deleted raises. Return nil when `embed.post` is blank, and consider destroying the orphaned row so the article can be re-imported.

- `<%- end if %>` compiles to a modifier-if whose condition is the next buffer append rather than closing the block cleanly. It happens to be truthy today, so only output order shifts, but the construct silently makes the header if/else depend on unrelated following code. Change it to `<%- end %>`, matching lines 22 and 28.

- The old `PostCreator` call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`; the new path does not, so imported topics take the import timestamp. Thread `created_at:` through `import_remote` / `import` -- `PostCreator` already supports it.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — `raw_html` cook method stores remote HTML verbatim and the view renders it with `raw`

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `raw_html` cook method (Post.cook_methods) and changes `Post#cook` to return `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). TopicEmbed.import/import_remote and Jobs::PollFeed create/update posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using content fetched from external sources (RSS `i.content` or remote HTML via open-uri). The embed view renders the result with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` and, for `raw_html`, `post.cooked` is effectively the unprocessed `post.raw`. This bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline and directly outputs remote HTML, creating a verifiable stored/served XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Embed URL interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted `href` in that same raw HTML

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it appends raw HTML to `contents` using `"#{url}"` inside an I18n string. `url` is only checked with `/^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or HTML-special characters. Because these imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (skipping sanitization) and later rendered via `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb`, a crafted URL containing `'` (or other payload) can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary HTML/JS (XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: - Any HTML in a polled feed becomes `post.cooked` unchanged and is emitted by `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20`, so a hostile or compromised feed serves scripts on the forum's own origin. The Readability path applies a tag allowlist; the RSS path applies nothing, which contradicts the stated intent that imported content must not escape validation. Put one `Sanitize.clean` (the `sanitize` gem is already a dependency) inside `TopicEmbed.import` with the allowlist the Readability path already uses, so every caller inherits it.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the feed item body is taken as `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed to `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`. Finally, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any `<script>`/event-handler HTML from a hostile or compromised feed would be stored and emitted as-is on the Discourse origin (at least within the embed iframe). The Readability path applies an allowlist (`tags`/`attributes`), but the RSS path does not, so the finding describes a real security problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - The `imported_from` footer builds `<a href='#{url}'>` with no escaping, and the only guard is the unanchored `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` on line 11, which permits a quote in the query string. A URL ending `?a='/onmouseover='alert(1)` breaks out of the attribute in a post whose output is rendered raw. Escape with `CGI.escapeHTML(url)` and tighten the guard to `URI.parse(url).is_a?(URI::HTTP)`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `"#{url}"` into `contents` with no escaping, and the only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows single quotes and other attribute-breaking characters in the remainder of the URL (e.g. query string). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that method, the HTML is rendered without sanitization (and the embed view uses `raw post.cooked`). A crafted URL like `http://example.com/?a='/onmouseover='alert(1)` would break out of the single-quoted `href` and inject attributes/JS, making this a verifiable XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — One malformed feed item aborts the whole hourly import

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then `TopicEmbed.import(...)` without any per-item error handling. If a feed item lacks `content` (i.content is nil) or contains data that makes `scrub`/`unescapeHTML` raise, a `NoMethodError`/exception will bubble up and abort the entire `poll_feed` run, preventing subsequent items from being imported that hour.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — Outer `Topic.transaction` swallows PostCreator's rollback; unsaved post passes `post.present?`

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `Topic.transaction` block does not itself “swallow” a rollback from `PostCreator` in any verifiable way based on this diff. The claim depends on undocumented behavior inside `PostCreator.create` (e.g., that it uses `ActiveRecord::Rollback` internally and returns an unsaved-but-non-nil post), which is not shown here. From the diff alone, the only observable fact is that it checks `post.present?`, but whether an unsaved post could be returned is speculative without seeing `PostCreator.create`’s implementation. Therefore the proposed finding is not a concrete, verifiable problem in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — `TopicEmbed.import_remote` has no test coverage at all

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) and the new specs cover `TopicEmbed.import` but do not directly exercise `import_remote`. However, “no test coverage” is a process/quality observation rather than a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff, so it doesn’t qualify as a real, verifiable problem under the given criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65 — `absolutize_urls` rewrites protocol-relative `//host/path` into a broken same-host URL

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links/images are rewritten whenever the attribute `start_with?('/')`. That condition matches both root-relative paths like `/foo` and protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/foo`. The rewrite uses `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, which strips both leading slashes from `//cdn...` to `cdn...`, then prefixes it with the source site `prefix` (scheme://host[:port]) producing `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/foo`, which is a broken same-host URL instead of preserving the protocol-relative external URL. This is directly verifiable from the diff logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column` with NOT NULL + default rewrites the whole `posts` table under lock

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that runs `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions commonly used at the time (and in general prior to PG 11), adding a column with a non-NULL default causes a full table rewrite and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration. Since `posts` is typically a very large/hot table, this is a real deploy-time risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` added to an already-shipped migration -- emits `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) by changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` causes the migration to issue a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` before creating the table. If this migration is executed against a database where `top_topics` already exists for any reason (e.g., schema drift, partially applied migrations, or a recreated DB with missing schema_migrations entries), it will drop the table and any data in it. This is a real, verifiable behavior change introduced by the diff and is potentially destructive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Disqus import silently drops `--category` / `-c` support

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Disqus Thor task option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes all logic that reads `options[:category]` to look up a `category_id` and pass it into `PostCreator`. The import now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` without any category parameter. As a result, users can no longer specify `--category`/`-c` when running the Disqus import, and imported topics will not be placed into a chosen category via that flag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — On-demand retrieval runs the entire hourly `PollFeed` job inline **(decision gate)**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` can synchronously fetch and parse the entire configured feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterate/import all items. This means an on-demand retrieval path (triggered when an embed is missing) runs the full scheduled feed-polling work inline, which is verifiable in the diff and is a concrete performance/side-effect defect (unnecessary heavy work per retrieval, not just for the single embed_url).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34 — Spec stubs the very methods it names in its test titles

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the examples are testing `TopicRetriever#retrieve`’s control flow (whether it calls `perform_retrieve`), and they stub `retrieved_recently?` to force the two branches. That’s a common unit-testing technique for isolating behavior and doesn’t indicate a functional bug or defect introduced by the diff. The spec is not “broken” or unverifiable; at most it’s a test design/style preference (mocking internals), not a real problem in the code change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:19 — Two guard tests pass regardless of the guard they claim to test

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed runs only if feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub one condition to nil, but do not stub the other two conditions to truthy values. Given the defaults added in config/site_settings.yml (feed_polling_enabled: false and the strings default to ''), poll_feed would be skipped anyway even if execute stopped checking feed_polling_url or embed_by_username—so those two tests can pass vacuously and don’t actually verify the claimed guards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` is never executed by any spec

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, which explicitly expects `poll_feed` to be called from `execute` (`poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`), but it does not exercise the *implementation* of `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (it never calls the real method body). However, that is a test coverage observation rather than a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the diff; the code can function correctly even if `poll_feed`’s internals aren’t covered by specs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — Iframe URL breaks when the integrator's `discourseUrl` has no trailing slash

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the iframe src is built via simple concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. This assumes `discourseUrl` ends with a trailing `/`. If an integrator sets `discourseUrl` to something like `https://forum.example.com` (no trailing slash), the result becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is an invalid path/host combination. The diff contains no normalization (e.g., ensuring a `/` between base and path), so the issue is real and directly verifiable from the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Unauthenticated endpoint drives unbounded outbound fetches and topic creation

adjudication.rationale: The new `GET /embed/best` endpoint does not require authentication (`current_user` can be nil) and, when an embed is not yet present, it enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (EmbedController#best). That job calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which can perform outbound HTTP fetches (`open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) and create new topics/posts (`TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator`) for any `embed_url` on the configured `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Throttling is only per-`embed_url` key for 60 seconds (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so a client can generate unbounded distinct URLs on the same host to trigger unbounded job enqueues, outbound fetches, and topic creation. The referer check in `ensure_embeddable` is header-based and does not provide authentication/robust abuse prevention against non-browser clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `Kernel#open` on an unvalidated String reaches the pipe/file fallback

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` after `require 'open-uri'`. Passing an arbitrary, unvalidated String into `Kernel#open` is dangerous because `open` supports non-HTTP targets (e.g., local file paths) and the pipe form (`"|cmd"`) which can execute a shell command via the pipe fallback. The diff only checks `feed_polling_url.present?` and does not validate it as an http(s) URL before calling `open`, so the described issue is verifiably present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — RSS content stored and rendered as unsanitized HTML

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` the feed item body is taken as `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed directly to `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This means HTML from the RSS/Atom feed can be stored and rendered as-is, enabling XSS if the feed contains malicious markup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `import_remote` has no rescue or timeout on the live fetch path

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does a live network fetch via `open(url).read` (from `open-uri`) and immediately parses it, but there is no `rescue` for network/HTTP/URI errors and no explicit timeout parameters passed to `open`. This means transient failures (DNS, connection errors, slow/hanging responses, invalid URL content) will raise exceptions and/or potentially block for extended periods in the background job paths that call `import_remote` (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, Disqus import). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can leave a TTL-less key that locks a URL out forever

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic; if the process crashes or errors after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be created without a TTL. After that, `setnx` will always fail and the method will always return `true` (treating it as “retrieved recently”), effectively blocking retrieval for that embed_url indefinitely (except when `no_throttle` is set).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — An exception from the inline feed poll prevents `fetch_http` from ever running

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline and only proceeds to `fetch_http` afterward. There is no `begin/rescue` around this call. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and parsing (`SimpleRSS.parse`) without error handling, either of which can raise. If an exception occurs, it will bubble up and abort `perform_retrieve`, so the fallback `fetch_http` path will not run. This is directly implied by the control flow in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:52 — A permanently-failing embed URL leaves the iframe looping and re-queuing jobs

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil it always enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url) and renders the loading template. app/views/embed/loading.html.erb reloads the iframe every 30 seconds via document.location.reload(). If the embed URL can never be imported (e.g., unreachable/404/parse error), topic_id will remain nil forever, so the iframe will reload indefinitely and each reload will enqueue another retrieve_topic job. TopicRetriever’s throttling only prevents repeated retrieval work inside a job (via Redis), but it does not prevent repeated job enqueuing from the controller, so the queue can grow continuously in this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `rss.items.each` has no rescue and calls `i.content.scrub` unconditionally. An RSS 2.0 item carrying only `<description>` gives `nil.scrub`, and one such item abandons every remaining item for that hourly run. Fall back across `content` / `description`, skip blank bodies, and wrap the loop body in rescue/next. Note `String#scrub` needs Ruby 2.1, so drop it or guard it.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `i.content.scrub` is called unconditionally and will fail when `i.content` is nil (common when feeds only provide `<description>`), and it explicitly recommends falling back to `description` to avoid crashes—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - Wrapping `PostCreator#create` in an outer `Topic.transaction` makes the inner transaction a joined, non-savepoint one, so the `ActiveRecord::Rollback` PostCreator raises is swallowed and `create` still returns the unsaved post. `post.present?` is then true and `TopicEmbed.create!` inserts `post_id: nil` into a `null: false` column. Drop the outer transaction and test `post.persisted?`, not `post.present?`.

- `import_remote` is reached only from `topic_retriever.rb:52` and `disqus.thor:148`, and no spec touches it, so the Readability wiring and the `opts[:title] || doc.title` branch are entirely unexercised. Add a spec that stubs the fetch and asserts `.import` receives the parsed title and content.

adjudication.rationale:
It’s accurate that `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is only invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, and the added specs cover `TopicEmbed.import`, `TopicRetriever.retrieve`, `EmbedController`, and `Jobs::PollFeed` but never call `import_remote`, so the `Readability::Document` parsing and `opts[:title] || doc.title` branch are unexercised.

However, this is a test coverage suggestion rather than a verifiable defect in correctness/security/behavior introduced by the diff. The diff does not show failing behavior due to the lack of a spec, only that the new code path isn’t tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `'//cdn.example.com/x.jpg'.start_with?('/')` is true, so a protocol-relative asset is rewritten to `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x.jpg` and every such image or link in imported content breaks. Add `&& !href.start_with?('//')` to both rewrites and cover the case.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and image rewrites run when href/src.start_with?('/') (and likewise for img src). Protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/x.jpg" also start with '/', so they match and are rewritten using "#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}", producing something like "http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x.jpg" instead of preserving the protocol-relative external URL. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the current logic and would break imported content containing protocol-relative asset/link URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - On the PostgreSQL 9.x this era targets, a NOT NULL column with a default forces a full rewrite under `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` on the largest table in a Discourse install. Split into add (nullable, no default), batched backfill reusing the retry loop already in `migrate_word_counts.rb`, then `change_column_null`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` that runs `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL 9.x, `ADD COLUMN` with a non-NULL default generally rewrites the whole table and takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock for the duration. Since `posts` is typically one of the largest tables in a Discourse install, this can cause a long blocking migration/downtime. The finding’s suggested mitigation (add nullable w/o default, backfill in batches, then enforce NOT NULL) directly addresses this real issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - This migration shipped before this branch; adding `force: true` makes it emit `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` on any `db:migrate:redo` or replay, silently destroying that table's data, while existing databases never re-run it at all. Revert the `force: true` -- it is a one-line deletion. If forcing is genuinely wanted, it belongs in a new timestamped migration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` causes `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` before creating the table. That changes the migration from “fail if the table already exists” to “silently drop and recreate it”, which can destroy any existing `top_topics` data in scenarios where the migration is re-run against a DB that already has the table (e.g., db:migrate:redo or an inconsistent environment). This destructive behavior is directly introduced by the one-line change in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and the category lookup, and `import_remote` threads no category anywhere, so existing `-c` invocations now fail as an unknown switch and imported topics land uncategorized. Thread an optional `category:` through `import_remote` and `import` into the internal `PostCreator.new`.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and the associated lookup of `category_id`. Thor will therefore treat existing `-c/--category` usage as an unknown option and fail. Additionally, the new import path `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` does not accept or pass any category information, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostCreator.new` without a `category:` option, so imported topics will default to whatever the app’s default/uncategorized behavior is. This is a concrete behavior regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - **Decision gate.** A single embed lookup re-downloads and re-upserts the entire feed inside a per-request worker, and the `feed_key` defined at `poll_feed.rb:20` that would make a conditional fetch possible is never used. Two defensible directions: drop the RSS pre-check and let `fetch_http` handle single-URL retrieval, or keep it and finish `feed_key` as a Last-Modified/ETag guard. Pick one before the rest of this group is worth optimizing.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), which in turn downloads and parses the entire feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each entry (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This path can be triggered by a single missing-embed lookup (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` enqueued from `EmbedController#best`), meaning a single embed URL retrieval may re-poll and re-process the whole feed. Also, `PollFeed#feed_key` is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff, so any intended conditional-fetch/throttling logic using that key is currently absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `topic_retriever_spec.rb:33-34` and `:39-40` stub both `perform_retrieve` and `retrieved_recently?`, so the test named for the throttle never runs the redis logic and nothing ever executes `perform_retrieve`. Stub the collaborators instead and assert the real outcome.

adjudication.rationale: The cited spec does intentionally mock/stub `retrieved_recently?` and set expectations on `perform_retrieve` to verify `TopicRetriever#retrieve` control flow (i.e., that it calls/doesn’t call `perform_retrieve` based on the boolean result). It’s true that this means the Redis throttling logic inside `retrieved_recently?` and the body of `perform_retrieve` are not executed by these examples, but that is a test-coverage/design choice, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. Also, the claim that “nothing ever executes perform_retrieve” is not a functional bug; the test explicitly asserts the call occurs (via `expects(:perform_retrieve).once`) rather than running its implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false, so `execute`'s guard short-circuits on the first condition; both tests would still pass with the `feed_polling_url` and `embed_by_username` checks deleted. Stub the preceding conditions to true in each test so it isolates the condition it names.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` only runs if `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the tests named "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub `feed_polling_url` or `embed_by_username` respectively, but do not stub the preceding condition `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`. Since the diff adds `feed_polling_enabled: false` as the default in `config/site_settings.yml`, `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` will be false unless overridden, causing the guard to short-circuit before evaluating the URL/username checks. Therefore those tests would still pass even if the `feed_polling_url.present?` / `embed_by_username.present?` checks were removed, meaning they don't actually verify the condition they claim to test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - Every spec replaces `poll_feed` with a mock, so the fetch, parse, and per-item import logic has zero executed coverage -- which is why defects #4, #17, and #19 are invisible to CI. Add a fixture-driven spec covering a normal item, a blank-link item, and a non-http link.

adjudication.rationale: The added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only exercises `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` by stubbing settings and mocking `poll_feed`; it does not execute the actual `poll_feed` implementation (open-uri fetch, `SimpleRSS.parse`, link/id fallback, per-item `TopicEmbed.import`). However, this is a test coverage critique, not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. The references to “defects #4, #17, and #19” are also not grounded in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` has no separator or normalization, and nothing in the diff documents a trailing-slash requirement, so an integrator setting `http://forum.example.com` silently gets `http://forum.example.comembed/best`. Strip trailing slashes and insert the `/` explicitly.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the iframe URL is built via simple concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. This only produces a valid path if `discourseUrl` already ends with `/`. Since `discourseUrl` is a global provided by the embedding integrator (not defined/normalized anywhere in this diff) and nothing here enforces or documents a trailing slash, a common configuration like `http://forum.example.com` would yield `http://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is a broken URL. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - Any request that passes the spoofable Referer check enqueues a retrieval, and the only throttle keys on the exact URL string, so varying query strings on the embeddable host yields unbounded outbound fetches and one new topic per distinct URL from unauthenticated callers. Add a `RateLimiter` keyed on `request.remote_ip` for anonymous callers and key the throttle on host as well as URL.

- Both `poll_feed.rb:29` and `topic_embed.rb:48` hand a String to `Kernel#open`, whose pipe and local-file fallbacks are reachable; the scheme check in `import` runs only after the fetch, and `disqus.thor:148` feeds it links parsed from an externally supplied Disqus XML export. Parse to a `URI::HTTP` first and pass the URI object, which removes the fallback entirely.
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags `poll_feed.rb` passing an unvalidated String to `Kernel#open`, enabling attacker-controlled fetching of arbitrary URLs (and even local-file/pipe fallbacks). This covers the golden issue: PollFeed uses `open(feed_polling_url)` without validating the URL, allowing SSRF-style arbitrary internal/external requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - The feed path CGI-unescapes raw content and stores it as a `raw_html` post with no `Sanitize` call anywhere, even though the gem is already a dependency. Same fix as #1; doing it once in `TopicEmbed.import` covers both.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code takes `i.content`, does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no `Sanitize` (or other HTML sanitization) applied anywhere in this RSS path, so arbitrary HTML from the feed can be stored and rendered as-is, creating a verifiable XSS/security risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `open(url).read` has no rescue and no explicit timeouts on the request-driven path. OpenURI raises on any non-2xx, a routine outcome for an arbitrary embed URL, so the job crashes and retries instead of returning nil, and `fetch_http` has no way to record a permanent failure. Rescue network and parse errors, set timeouts, and return nil.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds network fetching via OpenURI without error handling or timeouts. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, it does `open(url).read` (and in `Jobs::PollFeed`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) with no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` and no `rescue`. These calls can raise routinely (DNS failure, timeout, non-2xx HTTP responses, invalid content), and in the request-driven embed path `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#fetch_http -> TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Any exception will bubble up and fail the Sidekiq job; `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` does not set `retry: false`, so default retries are likely, and there is no mechanism in `fetch_http`/`import_remote` to record a permanent failure or gracefully return `nil` on fetch/parse errors. This is a concrete reliability defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - SETNX and EXPIRE are two separate commands; a crash or connection error between them leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no TTL, so `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever and that URL can never be imported again. Use the atomic `$redis.set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)` -- redis 3.0.6 in the lockfile supports it -- and release the key when the work fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or the Redis connection drops after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is applied, the key `retrieved:<url>` can be left without a TTL. In that state, subsequent calls will hit the `setnx` failure path and `retrieved_recently?` will return `true` indefinitely (for non-`no_throttle` callers), preventing `perform_retrieve` from ever running for that URL again. This is a real correctness/robustness issue introduced by the diff; using an atomic SET with NX+EX would avoid it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs unguarded before `fetch_http`, so any exception from the feed fetch, parse, or a single malformed item propagates and the on-demand HTTP retrieval never runs. Wrap the opportunistic poll in rescue-and-log, or enqueue it asynchronously.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously and without any `rescue`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network IO (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`), parsing (`SimpleRSS.parse`), and per-item processing (`i.content.scrub`, `CGI.unescapeHTML`, etc.), any of which can raise (e.g., OpenURI/network errors, parse errors, nil `i.content` causing `NoMethodError`). If an exception is raised, it will propagate out of `perform_retrieve` and `fetch_http` will never run, defeating the intended fallback behavior. This is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - Nothing records that a URL can never be imported, so the controller re-enqueues on every reload and the iframe loops on the loading view indefinitely. Persist a failure marker alongside the existing throttle key and render a distinct error view when it is set.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`. The loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) forces a `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds. If the embed can’t ever be imported (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early because `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is unset/invalid, or `open(url)`/Readability parsing fails and no `TopicEmbed` record is created), then `topic_id_for_embed` will remain nil forever. Nothing in the diff persists a permanent failure state or renders an error page, so the iframe can loop indefinitely and will keep re-enqueuing jobs on each reload (even if the job itself throttles HTTP fetches, the controller still enqueues repeatedly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — `postMessage` origin check is a substring test, not an origin match
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: the `postMessage` origin validation uses a substring/indexOf check rather than an exact origin match, allowing malicious lookalike domains (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`) to bypass the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Host-validation rule implemented twice, two different ways

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows host checks in two places, but they validate different inputs for different purposes: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` validates the *request referer* host before allowing iframe embedding, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` validates the *embed_url parameter* host before fetching/importing remote content. This is not the same rule duplicated “two different ways”; it’s defense-in-depth on two separate attack surfaces, and no correctness/security defect is directly introduced by having both checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:29 — `URI::InvalidURIError` rescue branch is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the code explicitly rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` (triggered by `URI(request.referer || '').host`) and raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The added controller spec covers missing referer (`nil`) and a valid referer URL, but it does not include any case where `request.referer` is a malformed URI that would actually raise `URI::InvalidURIError`. So the rescue branch introduced in this diff is not exercised by the tests in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25 — `embed_by_username` user lookup duplicated in two files

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain two similar lookups of the “embed by username” user: in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (`User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`) and in `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` with the same pattern. However, this is just code duplication/refactoring opportunity, not a verifiable bug, security issue, correctness problem, or clear defect introduced by the diff. Both lookups are contextually appropriate (feed polling vs HTTP fetch) and there’s no functional error demonstrated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8 — Loading page reloads every 30s forever with no cap or backoff

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the inline script calls setTimeout(() => document.location.reload(), 30000). Because this page is reloaded into itself, the same script runs again after each reload, creating an unbounded polling loop with a fixed 30s interval and no maximum retries/backoff. If the embed job never succeeds (or is disabled/misconfigured), it will reload forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — One dead thread link aborts the rest of the Disqus import

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import loop now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` for each thread. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` without any rescue. If a single Disqus thread link is dead/invalid or the request fails (e.g., `OpenURI::HTTPError`, timeouts, DNS errors), the exception will bubble up and terminate the Thor task, aborting the remainder of the threads in the loop. Previously the code didn’t fetch the remote URL, so this failure mode is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:50 — `TopicView.expects(:new)` never verifies the view is actually assigned

adjudication.rationale: The cited line in `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` is a test assertion choice, not a verifiable defect in the diff. In `EmbedController#best`, the code explicitly assigns `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`. The spec’s `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` already verifies the constructor call occurs with the expected arguments, and there is no evidence in the diff that `@topic_view` might not be assigned. Not checking `assigns(:topic_view)` is a potential test-strengthening suggestion, but it does not identify a real bug/security/correctness problem introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40 — `content_sha1`-unchanged branch and the `skip_validations` bypass are unproven

adjudication.rationale: The spec at spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only exercises the changed-content update path (where content_sha1 differs) and the creation path. It does not test the no-op branch (content_sha1 unchanged) nor does it assert that skip_validations changes save behavior, but that is a test-coverage observation rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. Nothing in the diff indicates those branches are incorrect; they’re simply untested here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — Public 1-minute cache applied to the loading page too

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally at the end of the action, even when no `topic_id` is found and the action does `render 'loading'`. That means the loading response will carry the same 1-minute cache headers as the normal embed page, which can cause clients/intermediaries to cache and continue serving the loading page briefly even after the topic becomes available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Feed fetch has no timeout or response-size cap

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the feed is fetched via `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (using open-uri) with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options and no limit on bytes read. A slow or unresponsive server can cause the scheduled job to hang, and an unusually large response can cause excessive memory/bandwidth usage, since the code blindly downloads and parses whatever comes back.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:35 — Re-import raises when the previously imported post was deleted

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` row is found (`embed` not blank), the code does `post = embed.post` and, if the content SHA1 changed, immediately does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. If the previously imported post was deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil` (dangling `post_id`), so `PostRevisor.new(nil)` / subsequent calls will raise (e.g., NoMethodError inside PostRevisor). There is no nil-guard or cleanup of the stale TopicEmbed record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` reads an unbounded remote document into memory

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`, which downloads the entire remote response body and reads it fully into a Ruby string with no size limit or streaming. This is a verifiable resource-consumption/DoS risk: a large (or infinite/slow) response can cause excessive memory usage or hang the process.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — Stray `<%- end if %>` turns the header block into a modifier-if
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Imported Disqus topics lose their original `created_at`

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the importer previously created the topic’s first post via `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)`, preserving the Disqus thread timestamp. The diff removes that and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post with `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` but does not pass `created_at` (nor is it set elsewhere), so the imported topic/post will use the current time, losing the original `created_at` from Disqus.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` searches the wrong direction and matches on substrings, so a shorter attacker origin contained in the URL passes. Normalize `discourseUrl` to a bare origin once, compare with `!==`, and also check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

- The reload is unconditional with no attempt cap, and each reload re-enqueues a job, so a URL that can never import polls forever. Cap at roughly five attempts and render a link to the forum instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no max-attempt limit. Therefore, if the embed can never be created (e.g., import fails, invalid `embed_url` host, network errors, etc.), the iframe will reload forever and each reload will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job. While `TopicRetriever` has a 60s throttle for retrieval work, it does not prevent repeated job enqueuing or the infinite reload loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` runs after both branches, so a shared cache can serve "Loading Discussion..." for a minute after the topic exists. Move it inside the `if topic_id` branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after both branches. When `topic_id` is nil, the action enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders the `loading` template, but that response will still be marked cacheable for 1 minute. For the same `embed_url` query, a browser/proxy/shared cache can legitimately reuse the cached “Loading Discussion...” response for up to a minute even after the topic has been created, delaying the appearance of the actual embed content. This is directly implied by the control flow in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - The update branch calls `PostRevisor.new(embed.post)` with no nil check, so re-importing an article whose post was deleted raises. Return nil when `embed.post` is blank, and consider destroying the orphaned row so the article can be re-imported.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `post = embed.post` and, if the content changed, unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. There is no guard for `embed.post` being nil. Since the migration only adds an index and no foreign key constraints, and the associations in `TopicEmbed` do not declare `dependent:` cleanup, it is plausible for a `topic_embeds` row to remain after the associated `Post` is deleted, making `embed.post` nil and causing an exception when re-importing that URL. The finding correctly points to a concrete nil-dereference risk in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `<%- end if %>` compiles to a modifier-if whose condition is the next buffer append rather than closing the block cleanly. It happens to be truthy today, so only output order shifts, but the construct silently makes the header if/else depend on unrelated following code. Change it to `<%- end %>`, matching lines 22 and 28.
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using `<%- end if %>` is incorrect for closing an ERB `if` block and should be replaced with `<%- end %>`. The candidate explains the miscompilation/semantics, but it’s the same underlying issue and fix as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - The old `PostCreator` call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`; the new path does not, so imported topics take the import timestamp. Thread `created_at:` through `import_remote` / `import` -- `PostCreator` already supports it.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the old import path created the first post with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`. The new code replaces that with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. In the added `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `.import`, neither method passes a `created_at` to `PostCreator` (it only passes `title`, `raw`, `skip_validations`, `cook_method`), so the post/topic will get the current time instead of the original Disqus thread timestamp. This is a verifiable behavior regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — Unused `require_dependency 'email/sender'`

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the file requires `require_dependency 'email/sender'` but the class `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` never references `Email::Sender` (it only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`). This makes the `email/sender` require unused/unnecessary in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — `feed_key` defined but never called -- the conditional fetch it implies is unimplemented

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the `feed_key` method is indeed defined and not referenced anywhere in the added job (nor in this diff). However, this is just unused/dead code; it does not create a functional bug, security issue, or correctness defect by itself. The claim that it implies an “unimplemented conditional fetch” is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:62 — Near-identical `a[href]` / `img[src]` rewrite loops

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, there are two similar loops: one rewrites `` `href` attributes and the other rewrites `` `src` attributes when they start with '/'. This is some duplication, but it is not a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff: each loop targets a different tag/attribute, and the logic is consistent and functional as written. The finding is essentially a style/DRY maintainability nit rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:37 — Unused `embed.permalink` locale key

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and none of the newly added code in this diff references that key (the views use `embed.title`, `embed.start_discussion`, `embed.continue`, `embed.loading`, and `embed.imported_from`). However, an “unused locale key” is not a verifiable correctness/security defect (I18n will not error on extra keys), and it also can’t be conclusively proven unused across the whole codebase from this diff alone.
